_premise: A showcase for a design skill is a claim, and a claim has to be checked. This site sets each arm as a printer's proof: one pull on uncoated white stock, marked in one sky-blue accent, crop marks at the corners, the measurement written in the margin in mono. The proof is pulled against an open sky — a live Cloudscape hero behind the thesis — and everything below it resolves on scroll the way a plate is lowered onto a light table.
_note: Authored in OKLCH (see design/palette.py, which round-trips through skills/parti/scripts/color.py). Hex below is the exact sRGB round-trip, for tooling only. Every text pair is contrast-verified against every ground it actually renders on; the verification is a build step, not a claim.

_type.interface: Geist — everything structural: navigation, prose, controls, and the thesis lines.
_type.evidence: Geist Mono — labels, plate numbers, measurements, tokens, code, crop-mark coordinates.
_type._why: A printer's proof has no editorial display face — the argument is carried by size and the accent, not a change of voice. Two faces, one job each.

_shape._why: Crop marks and registration marks meet at right angles; a rounded corner is not something a proof has. Applies everywhere, including buttons and inputs.
_shape._exception: The radio-button dot and the switch thumb stay rounded-full — their circular shape is the control's meaning, not decoration. The one other exception is the hero Cloudscape, the single soft surface in the system; it is never itself framed.

_elevation._why: A drop shadow on one pane of a two-pane comparison adds visual weight to that pane. The instrument must not put its thumb on the scale.

_motion.libraries: framer-motion (motion) for React enter/exit and micro-interactions; gsap + ScrollTrigger + @gsap/react for scroll reveals and the two Geist text treatments; Cloudscape ships its own WebGL rAF loop.
_motion.the_one_choreographed_moment: the hero — Cloudscape drifting behind while pixel-text-fill resolves the thesis on load
_motion.the_one_direct_manipulation_moment: the comparison slider — it tracks the pointer 1:1 with no easing, because a lagging divider makes the two arms look misaligned when they are not
_motion.scroll_reveal: one shared Reveal primitive: opacity 0→1 + y 16px→0, 480ms power2.out, ScrollTrigger start 'top 80%', once: true, ~60ms child stagger
_motion.never_animates: anything that repeats on every scroll pass; parallax on the plates (only the hero sky moves); the margin-rail numbers; focus rings
